video_title: The Rapping Chef On His Viral Journey, Cooking for T-Mac & Carving Out His Own Lane | Cousins

quotes.speaker: Josh
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh on his journey from shy rapper to viral cooking content creator
quotes.excerpt: I was super shy in my early twenties when I started rapping. I love to do it.
quotes.quote: I was super shy in my early twenties when I started rapping. I love to do it, but I didn't want to do it in front of people. I guess in fear of being critiqued. I get to my mid-twenties now and nothing is really happening, so I kind of just fell back. And then I moved to Houston. I started cooking for my brother, and then at this time, this is COVID, so I'm seeing everyone on TikTok having fun. So I started doing it. I started doing regular cooking videos where you just narrate it regular and it was not getting no motion. So I switched it up and I started rapping the thing and I repurposed that rap stuff into some content.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on Josh finding a unique lane in content creation
quotes.excerpt: It's pretty dope when you see all the content that is put on social media.
quotes.quote: It's pretty dope when you see all the content that is put on social media and then you actually discovering, finding a lane to where you ain't got no competition. There is no competition and that to me surprised like, damn, is nobody out there doing that? When you search, there is nobody out there doing that.

quotes.speaker: Josh
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh on the importance of consistency in building his social media following
quotes.excerpt: It didn't really take, it just took consistency. I wasn't having many views even when I started rapping.
quotes.quote: It didn't really take, it just took consistency. I wasn't having many views even when I started rapping. I had more than when I was just talking like, hey, add two tablespoons of this, add a couple of this. I had more views than that, but I wasn't going viral. But I kept going and by that tenth video, I got maybe 700,000 views and that kind of put a battery in my back, so I was like, I'm going to keep doing this.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on the business side of being a content creator
quotes.excerpt: How does that work with content creators? Do you sign with an agency?
quotes.quote: How does that work with content creators? Do you sign with an agency and your agency is going out trying to find deals, sponsorships for you? Talk about the business side of being a content creator.

quotes.speaker: Josh
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh on the benefits of signing with a talent agency for content creators
quotes.excerpt: The good thing about signing with a talent agency is because you no longer have to negotiate.
quotes.quote: When you start out, you navigating it solo. So if you have a video that go viral, management companies will reach out like, hey, we want to represent you. But you don't really want to trust the first person. If a company or a brand reaches out, they want you to put their product in your video. You may accept what they offer because you don't know any better. A year in is when I signed with the talent agency and the good thing about signing with a talent agency is because you no longer have to negotiate. You no longer have to prospect and find your own deals and they are doing everything for you. And plus, they know your worth and you don't know it. I encourage anybody making content, definitely sign with an agency because if people know what they're talking about, you'd be selling yourself short if you're trying to do this on your own.

quotes.speaker: Josh
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh on the importance of consistent posting for algorithm success
quotes.excerpt: Now I'm repurposing old videos, so sometimes you might see me posting stuff, but it might be old.
quotes.quote: Now I'm repurposing old videos, so sometimes you might see me posting stuff, but it might be an old video. But I'm also posting new stuff as well. And like the algorithm changes so much, like if you take too much time off, they'll kind of penalize you for that and they won't push your your video out as much. So if you constantly posting stuff every day, the algorithm is going to keep you in in rotation. They're going to keep you in the loop. Now, if you post every week, you might you might not see the same the same numbers.

quotes.speaker: Josh
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh on the challenges of posting content and dealing with criticism
quotes.excerpt: People probably got videos in their phone right now that they worked hard to create.
quotes.quote: People probably got videos in their phone right now that they worked hard to create, but they're scared to post it and scared of being critiqued, which goes back to my thing about when I was trying to rap and I didn't want to put my music out. I didn't want to get on stage and do all this because I was afraid. But yeah, you have to just you got to be brave, man. You'll be rewarded. Just put the content out there because I know you have it.
